title: Probar el round-trip real de publicación de una página canary sin promover Current
mission: Prove the page pipeline beyond deterministic request convergence by exercising one isolated reversible canary through reserve/request -> build -> verify -> publish -> registry/watch consumption under the binding page protocols, while keeping Current/Human Accepted/Served authority unchanged.
definition_of_done: Load PAGE_PLATE_PROTOCOL_V1 and PAGE_REQUEST_PUBLICATION_PROTOCOL_V1 and use their exact reservation/publication laws.
Use an isolated reversible canary identity/path so the test cannot silently replace a real Current page.
Produce durable evidence for request/reservation, built bytes, verification result, publication commit and registry/watch consumption.
Verify the served canary in a representative browser and prove the Live shelf can discover/open it from static registry data.
After evidence is durable, leave either a clearly marked canary artifact or a reversible cleanup commit as the protocol permits; do not fabricate Human Accepted or promote Current.
If any authority boundary blocks the full path, return the exact bounded boundary instead of partially promoting state.
